title: Cognitive Dissonance Theory: A Summary
text:
Cognitive dissonance, first proposed by Leon Festinger, describes the mental discomfort experienced by an individual who simultaneously holds two or more contradictory beliefs, ideas, or values. This psychological inconsistency creates a state of tension that motivates the person to reduce the discrepancy.

The drive to achieve internal consistency often leads individuals to alter their thoughts or behaviors rather than accept the conflicting information. Reduction can occur through changing one's attitudes (e.g., minimizing the importance of the contradiction) or by adding new cognitions that justify the existing conflict, thereby restoring psychological equilibrium.

Effective strategies for resolving dissonance typically involve rationalization. For instance, a smoker who knows smoking is harmful might reduce dissonance not by quitting immediately, but by focusing on anecdotal evidence regarding perceived low risk, thus reinforcing the behavior through selective cognitive adjustment.
